en: Itivuttaka 88:
Tikanipāta, Catutthavagga (The Fourth Chapter)
The Discourse on the Internal Impurities.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:
"Bhikkhus, there are these three internal impurities, internal enemies, internal adversaries, internal murderers, and internal foes."
Which three?
Greed, monks, is an internal stain, an internal enemy, an internal adversary, an internal slayer, an internal opponent.
Hatred, monks, is an internal stain, an internal enemy, an internal adversary, an internal slayer, an internal opponent.
“Delusion, bhikkhus, is an internal stain, an internal enemy, an internal adversary, an internal slayer, an internal foe.
These, bhikkhus, are the three internal stains, internal enemies, internal adversaries, internal slayers, and internal foes.
Thus the Blessed One spoke this matter.
In this regard, it is said:
"Greed produces what is harmful;
greed agitates the mind."
Fear born from within,
people do not perceive it;
being greedy, one does not understand one's true welfare.
The greedy person does not see the Dhamma;
it is blinding darkness when greed overcomes a man.
But he who, having abandoned greed,
is not greedy for things that provoke greed—
greed is abandoned by him.
Like a drop of water on a lotus leaf.
Hatred produces misfortune;
hatred agitates the mind.
Fear born from within—
people do not perceive it;
one who is corrupted does not understand his own welfare.
One who is corrupted does not see the Dhamma;
it is utter darkness then when hatred overcomes a person.
But he who, having abandoned hatred,
does not hate that which provokes hatred—
hatred is abandoned by him.
Like a ripe palm fruit from its stalk,
so delusion produces harm;
delusion agitates the mind.
Fear born from within,
people do not perceive it;
deluded, they do not understand the true meaning.
One who is deluded does not see the Dhamma;
it is blinding darkness then,
when delusion overcomes a person.
But he who, having abandoned delusion,
is not bewildered by what causes delusion—
he destroys all delusion.
“Like the rising of the sun, [it dispels] the darkness.
This meaning too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The ninth [sutta].
